expected.title: fix(mr issue): limit concurrent lookups in bulk commands
expected.body:
Part 1 of 3 for https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8663.

## What

`MRsFromArgs` and `IssuesFromArgs` started one request per argument with no cap, so `glab mr close 1 2 3 … 200` sent 200 requests at once. Both errgroups now call `SetLimit(api.MaxConcurrentRequests)`, a new shared constant set to 5.

This affects `mr approve`, `close`, `delete`, `reopen`, `revoke`, `subscribe`, `unsubscribe` and `issue close`, `reopen`, `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `delete`.

`IssuesFromArgs` also stops writing `baseRepo` from every goroutine (a data race the new test exposed under `-race`). It now returns the last argument's repo instead of whichever goroutine finished last.

## Tests

`Test_MRsFromArgs_LimitsConcurrency` and `Test_IssuesFromArgs_LimitsConcurrency` block the stubbed GET, wait for 5 requests in flight, then release them and assert the peak was exactly 5. Both fail when `SetLimit` is removed.

## Before and after

I closed and then reopened 10 issues (`glab issue close "23,…,32" -R jay_mccure/test2target`), 5 rounds per binary, alternating. Both builds had the same temporary hook that logged when each HTTP request started and ended. It wasn't committed.

| | before (`main`) | after (this MR) |
|---|---|---|
| Most requests in flight at once | 10 | 5 |
| Lookup phase (10 GETs), median | 0.63s | 1.00s |
| Updates (10 PUTs, sequential), median | 8.4s | 8.2s |
| Whole command, median | 9.4s | 9.7s |

At most 5 requests now run at once instead of one per issue. The cost is about 0.4s more for the lookups, which is within run-to-run noise, because the sequential updates take most of the time. One "before" run had a single 134s GET (it still returned 200). That run is left out of the medians (including it moves them by less than 0.1s), because it was a slow response from GitLab, not something the limit affects.

## Follow-ups

- `glab api`: wait and retry on 429 (`Retry-After` / `RateLimit-Reset`), including between `--paginate` pages.
- `glab api`: retry 5xx for idempotent methods only.

Related to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8663

files.patch:
@@ -6,6 +6,8 @@ import (
 	"context"
 	"errors"
 	"fmt"
+	"strconv"
+	"sync/atomic"
 	"testing"
 	"time"
 
@@ -1357,3 +1359,50 @@ func Test_RebaseMR_StopsWaitingWhenContextIsCancelled(t *testing.T) {
 	require.ErrorIs(t, err, context.Canceled)
 	assert.Equal(t, 1, polls)
 }
+
+func Test_MRsFromArgs_LimitsConcurrency(t *testing.T) {
+	ios, _, _, _ := cmdtest.TestIOStreams()
+	f := cmdtest.NewTestFactory(ios, cmdtest.WithBaseRepo("foo", "bar", ""))
+
+	var inFlight, maxInFlight atomic.Int32
+	release := make(chan struct{})
+	origGetMR := api.GetMR
+	t.Cleanup(func() { api.GetMR = origGetMR })
+	api.GetMR = func(_ *gitlab.Client, _ any, mrID int64, _ *gitlab.GetMergeRequestsOptions) (*gitlab.MergeRequest, error) {
+		n := inFlight.Add(1)
+		defer inFlight.Add(-1)
+		for {
+			m := maxInFlight.Load()
+			if n <= m || maxInFlight.CompareAndSwap(m, n) {
+				break
+			}
+		}
+		<-release
+		return &gitlab.MergeRequest{BasicMergeRequest: gitlab.BasicMergeRequest{IID: mrID}}, nil
+	}
+
+	args := make([]string, 4*api.MaxConcurrentRequests)
+	for i := range args {
+		args[i] = strconv.Itoa(i + 1)
+	}
+
+	type result struct {
+		mrs []*gitlab.MergeRequest
+		err error
+	}
+	done := make(chan result)
+	go func() {
+		mrs, _, err := MRsFromArgs(t.Context(), f, args, "")
+		done <- result{mrs, err}
+	}()
+
+	require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
+		return inFlight.Load() == api.MaxConcurrentRequests
+	}, time.Second, time.Millisecond)
+	close(release)
+	res := <-done
+
+	require.NoError(t, res.err)
+	require.Len(t, res.mrs, len(args))
+	assert.Equal(t, int32(api.MaxConcurrentRequests), maxInFlight.Load())
+}
